review_metadata.review_question: Does the rendered Decision Work Brief answer what this process made the decision-maker see or do differently?
review_metadata.review_scope: One checked-in-safe provisional case only; no human review and no broad batch.

input_refs.content_boundary: reviewed as the existing internal maintainer/debug layer, not as a same-case customer brief
checked-in-safe provisional draft review with embedded lolla.decision_work_brief.v0 object
deterministic rendering of the embedded PR116 brief, without new semantic content

reviewed_artifacts.review_read: Useful as internal artifact/custody status, but it names machinery more than decision consequence.

reviewed_artifacts.artifact: PR116 structured Decision Work Brief draft
reviewed_artifacts.review_read: Contains the decision story and custody boundaries, but JSON shape is not a humane reading surface.
Makes the decision/action consequence easier to scan while preserving uncertainty, source status, custody flags, and non-claims.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name the decision in under 30 seconds?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The first section states the CEO/cofounder operating-leadership decision directly.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name the likely starting direction?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The rendered brief names a possible reset/cooperation-test starting path, but marks it high uncertainty because the raw baseline is absent.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name what Lolla pressed on?
usefulness_questions.rationale: Authority ambiguity, stop conditions, transition-role scope, and glossy role framing are visible.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name what changed?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The rendered brief names authority-first movement, narrower transition support, and stop-loss conditions.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name what action would be different now?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The action consequence says the CEO would align authority transfer and escalation triggers before the conversation.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name what still might be wrong?
usefulness_questions.rationale: Missing raw context, vanilla overlap, relationship risk, and legal/governance uncertainty are visible.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader name what was not proven?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The rendered brief has a dedicated not-proven section plus non-claims and custody flags.

usefulness_questions.question: Can a reader distinguish the brief from the receipt appendix?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The rendered brief starts with decision sections, but source refs and field-key labels still make it feel partly internal.

usefulness_questions.question: Does the brief feel useful, or merely impressive?
usefulness_questions.rationale: It is useful where it names action consequence, but still carries enough schema vocabulary to feel like a product-shape artifact.

usefulness_questions.question: Does the brief overclaim because the receipt is clean?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The rendered page is orderly enough that readers may overweight a one-case, non-human-validated draft.

usefulness_questions.question: Does the brief hide uncertainty?
usefulness_questions.rationale: High uncertainty and missingness are prominent in the starting-direction and remaining-risk sections.

usefulness_questions.question: Does the brief preserve source/missingness status without drowning the story?
usefulness_questions.rationale: The story comes first, but per-section source refs still add a lot of artifact language.

usefulness_questions.question: Does the brief avoid internal machinery labels?
usefulness_questions.rationale: Human-readable headings help, but field keys and artifact paths remain visible because PR117 is a conservative renderer.

usefulness_questions.question: Is the evidence too thin for a customer-facing example?
usefulness_questions.rationale: A customer-facing example should wait for either human review or at least a second tiny case because this artifact uses one Codex-assisted draft only.

readability_findings.strongest_useful_signal: The rendered brief clearly answers the action-consequence question: move authority first, narrow transition support, and set stop conditions before the cofounder conversation.
readability_findings.main_readability_gain_over_receipt_debug: The receipt debug summary explains artifact health and missingness; the brief explains what changed in the decision story.
readability_findings.main_readability_limit: Schema key names and source refs are still visible enough that the page reads like an internal product-shape artifact rather than final customer copy.

overclaim_findings.strongest_overclaim_risk: The Markdown format makes the one-case Codex-assisted read feel more complete than the source boundary permits.
overclaim_findings.why_it_matters: A reader could mistake clean custody and clear prose for proof that Lolla improved the decision.
overclaim_findings.mitigation_present: The rendered brief shows human validation false, product proof false, answer-quality scoring false, agent action authorization false, high uncertainty, missingness, and explicit non-claims.

evidence_support_findings.support_read: The rendered brief is grounded in checked-in-safe PR116 structured fields and PR117 deterministic rendering, but the underlying semantic read is still Codex-assisted and one-case only.
what_would_need_to_be_true_before_custom: At least one more diverse case should show the brief can name action consequence without overclaiming.
A human reviewer should check whether the starting direction and action delta are fair.
The renderer should reduce internal artifact language if the output is meant for customers.
The source boundary should remain visible enough that clean artifacts are not mistaken for good advice.

missingness_findings.strongest_missingness_thinness_risk: The review cannot know whether the starting direction, vanilla overlap, user intent, and lost-value severity are accurate because raw/private context is not checked in and no human review exists.
missingness_findings.same_case_receipt_debug_summary_gap: No same-case checked-in receipt debug summary was reviewed for the cofounder case; the comparison uses the receipt debug-summary contract and the PR117 rendered brief.
human_followup_needed: Did the CEO already intend to move authority before the Lolla-shaped draft?
Would an authority-first action overcorrect against trust, dignity, or customer continuity?
Were legal, equity, board, or employment constraints material but outside the checked-in-safe packet?

decision_gate.rationale: The rendered brief is useful enough to test once more, but one Codex-assisted checked-in-safe case is too thin for customer-facing example work or runtime planning.

blocked_outcomes.reason: Not justified after one non-human-validated case.
The brief does answer what changed, even if it still carries internal artifact language.

next_recommendation.recommended_next_pr: PR119 Decision Work Brief Second Tiny Case Pilot v0
next_recommendation.recommended_action: Repeat the PR115 to PR117 path on one additional diverse completed run, then compare whether the brief still names action consequence without hiding uncertainty.
do_not_do_next: Do not broaden to a batch.
Do not publish a customer-facing example.
Do not treat this one case as product proof.
